transcription: X-Wife lied about daughter, so to get the full picture you need a bit of background, I met my now X-Wife through friends when we were both 25, I'm now 42. She had a young daughter when we started dating, her X wasn't in the picture due to restraining orders and domestic violence. I was young, ignored some red flags with her behavior and we got married a year later. I raised my stepdaughter like my own, there was no drama with her father due to him living provinces away in the restraining orders. For the first two years things were fine but the red flags I had ignored started to pop up more and more. Erratic behavior, she'd be gone and have no good answer about where she was or what she was doing. Eventually it started to come out that she had developed an addiction. I knew she was a part of her before we got married but figured that was behind her. As time went on, money was missing, her behavior was all over the place, and it became very obvious she had addiction issues. I wasn't interested in being in that situation so we started a separation period. She eventually went into rehab voluntarily and my stepdaughter stayed with me. Fast forward a year after she finished rehab, we weren't rushing back to normal married life, my stepdaughter remained with me. She eventually came to me and told me she was pregnant. I was initially a bit hesitant because we weren't on steady footing together but we decided to try to work on things and keep our family intact. After our daughter was born, I noticed some of the same old patterns emerging and she was upfront that she had relapsed. She went back into rehab and came out in what seemed like a good place. We had three years of normal family life and I thought everything was behind us. Then the warning signs came back. It was all in her behavior. Could see she was clearly drinking during the day when I'd get home from work, found bottles of vodka hidden around our house but this time, she denied she was drinking or had any issues. She claimed they were old bottles, she was tired, stressed out, all the usual excuses you'd expect. It got to the point where I didn't trust her at home alone with a girl so I'd take my stepdaughter to school and her sister to a babysitter, which may have made me feel better but gave her nothing but time and space to do whatever she wanted during the day. Inevitably I'd get everyone home and she would be drunk, passed out, or worse up and trying to have conversations and acting like everything was normal. Kids aren't stupid and my stepdaughter could clearly tell her mom wasn't okay. Let's start at a string of rehabs in a pattern. She'd go to rehab, be asked to leave for breaking the rules, I'd pick her up, wait for the next rehab to be ready to do an intake and drop her off the course of a year she went through seven rehab centers, never completing a full program. What ended our marriage for good was when I spoke to a counselor at one rehab center and she informed she had been asked to leave for inappropriate sexual behavior with two other patients. I was busy raising our kids, paying for rehab, paying our mortgage, supporting her in any way I could and that's what I got in return. Now risky behavior is part of addiction I've come to learn so I wasn't surprised. After her last failed rehab, I let her know she couldn't stay with us anymore and had to figure this out on her own. It sounds cold but I couldn't compromise my kids or my own well-being anymore. From then on she moved to a large city five hours away and spiraled into drugs, had stints of homelessness, jail time, and over the next eight years only saw our kids a handful of time. I ended up adopting my stepdaughter and taking all the steps I needed to so they'd remain with me and be in a stable environment. After eight years with very limited contact my kids went with their grandparents to their mother's city for an unrelated shopping trip while unbeknown to me their grandparents arranged to see their daughter and my kids mother. It was during this trip that my ex-wife decided to tell my youngest daughter that I wasn't her biological father. I found out from a text from my ex-mother-in-law. Obviously I've gone through all the emotions, anger for not being informed of them meeting in advance, for my ex dropping something like that on both of us with no discussion, sadness at the thought of my daughter not being mine. So we are currently awaiting the results of a paternity test to figure out what our next steps are. Being separated when she got pregnant I'm not sure if I should be surprised by this but I was the only one she said she'd been sleeping with during that time yes stupid to sleep with someone unprotected when you're separated and I was the one to be there for the birth.
